sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Trump Unveils Revised Washington D.C. Arch Plans
cards.content: The Trump administration has released final plans for a 250-foot triumphal arch in Washington D.C., but without the military complex features that President Donald Trump initially proposed. The new documents describe the arch as a 'ceremonial gateway' rather than a national security purpose. The project, which would sit near Arlington National Cemetery, has been met with opposition from preservationists and veterans who are concerned about the impact it would have on the cemetery's solemnity and the sightline of national landmarks. The Interior Department has stated that the current design of the arch is capable of accommodating the national security functions, but the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation will need to review the use of the arch as a military asset separately from the construction plans. The project has received preliminary approval from the National Capital Planning Commission and is eyeing approval in November.

cards.title: Israeli Settlers Attack European Diplomats in West Bank, EU and US Condemn
cards.content: A delegation of European diplomats from Belgium, France, Poland, and the Catholic Church was attacked by masked Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank. The attackers smashed a car window, assaulted a French mayor, and confronted the convoy. The Belgian government condemned the assault, calling on Israel to bring the perpetrators to justice. The Israeli Defense Forces also condemned the attack, saying they were investigating. However, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office questioned the incident, suggesting it was part of a 'coordinated campaign to smear Israel.' The US Secretary of State and Ambassador to Israel also condemned the attack, calling it 'disturbing' and 'despicable.' This incident is part of a series of attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians and diplomats in the West Bank, with some calling for EU sanctions against those responsible.

cards.title: 17 Killed in Crush at Kolkata Hindu Festival Amid Sudden Rain
cards.content: At least 17 people died and many more were injured in a crush at a Hindu festival event in Kolkata, India, after sudden rainfall caused a surge of people seeking shelter. A 7-year-old girl was among the dead, and 25 people were treated for injuries. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the incident as 'tragic' and pledged support to affected families. The crush occurred after an announcement caused 'commotion' among the crowd, leading to a stampede. This tragic incident is not the first of its kind in India, where poor management and lack of safety precautions have led to deadly crowd incidents during religious festivals.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: SpaceX Delivers Cargo to International Space Station
cards.content: In a mission that could lead to new medical breakthroughs, SpaceX successfully delivered a cargo of scientific experiments and supplies to the International Space Station. The Dragon spacecraft, launched on October 13, arrived at the station on October 15 and brought over 6,300 pounds of cargo, including tiny brain models, artificial retina technology, and 3D heart tissue. The experiments aim to advance medical research on Earth, with one focusing on manufacturing artificial retinas and another using 3D heart tissue models to test large-scale drug testing. The spacecraft will remain docked at the station until mid-November before returning to Earth, concluding its mission with a splashdown off the California coast.

cards.title: NASA Backs Lunar Cave Search to Reveal Moon's Volcanic History
cards.content: NASA is backing a project to search for a hidden lunar cave, which could reveal how ancient volcanic activity shaped the Moon. The project, led by the Planetary Science Institute, will use a lander and rover to investigate a potential large cave near the Marius Hill Pit. The team will employ ground-penetrating radar, seismic sensors, and gravity measurements to gather data, and if successful, the discovery could provide insights into the Moon's volcanic history and potentially even shelter astronauts from radiation and extreme temperatures. The project is funded by NASA's Payloads and Research Investigations on the Surface of the Moon program and is expected to provide valuable information about the Moon's subsurface and geology.

cards.title: Ancient Insect Found with Bendy Straw Feeding Organ in Amber
cards.content: Researchers have discovered a 99-million-year-old insect, Cretodorus noonoo, that had an ancient adaptation of a flexible and durable feeding organ, resembling a bendy straw, which allowed it to feed on tree sap. The newly described species, found in Myanmar, had mouthparts nearly twice the length of its body and was preserved in amber. The unique feature of the insect's mouthparts was densely covered with crosswise folds, which likely allowed it to bend and flex without collapsing. This discovery provides a glimpse into the insect world during the age of dinosaurs, and suggests that ancient forests created ecological conditions and opportunities very different from those we know today.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Cancer drug works by blocking DHODH, not KDM4
cards.content: Researchers have found that a cancer drug, zavondemstat, works mainly by blocking an enzyme called DHODH, rather than targeting KDM4 as originally thought. This discovery has implications for understanding how earlier studies using a related compound, QC6352, may need to be reinterpreted. The team developed new compounds that inhibit KDM4 without affecting DHODH, allowing scientists to study KDM4's role more accurately. The findings raise questions about whether clinical trials for zavondemstat are being designed around the correct biological mechanism.

cards.title: MDS patients have lower bone density and poorer survival
cards.content: For people with myelodysplastic syndromes, a type of blood cancer, osteoporosis may be an important clue to survival. Researchers found that patients with MDS had significantly lower bone density and continued to lose bone mass over time. Patients with osteoporosis at the beginning of the study also had poorer overall survival. The study suggests that bone health, often overlooked in MDS care, may reveal important information about patients' overall health and prognosis. The findings highlight the need to consider bone health when diagnosing and managing MDS, particularly for older adults with complex conditions. This could lead to new ways to investigate how blood formation, aging, and bone metabolism influence one another.

cards.title: Fat Before Carbs Regulates Blood Sugar in Mice Study
cards.content: In a breakthrough study, researchers found that eating fat before carbohydrates can help regulate blood sugar levels by slowing down stomach emptying and reducing the initial spike. This effect was observed in mice and may be applicable to humans, offering a potential dietary strategy to manage post-meal blood sugar rises, an important treatment target in diabetes.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: NASA captures rare atmospheric waves above Hurricane Simon
cards.content: NASA captured rare atmospheric waves above Hurricane Simon as it moved along Mexico's Pacific coast. Although the storm stayed offshore, it brought heavy rainfall and strong winds, causing flooding and landslides. Meanwhile, NASA satellites detected enormous ripples in the upper atmosphere, a phenomenon caused by the storm's powerful winds and heat release. These ripples can travel far above the storm, reaching the stratosphere and mesosphere. The NASA VIIRS instrument detected this phenomenon due to the Moon providing very little illumination, allowing the faint atmospheric glow to stand out. cards.title: Avalanche Sweeps Away Over 100 Sheep in Himachal Pradesh
cards.content: In October 2025, Joginder Chand, a 50-year-old shepherd from Himachal Pradesh's Chamba district, set out to migrate his 600 sheep and goats to warmer grazing grounds in Kangra district. Suddenly, an avalanche swept away over 100 animals.

cards.title: Srinagar's Water Crisis Worsens due to Climate Change
cards.content: In Srinagar, a water crisis has been ongoing for years, causing daily struggles for residents like Mehak and Zamrood. The absence of a regular water supply has led to the installation of tanks and a hand pump at their homes. Climate change is affecting Doodh Ganga, a vital source of drinking water, causing erratic water supply, low flow, and dry taps. The river's water availability is decreasing due to rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and declining snowmelt. The Kashmir Valley's 24 watersheds, including Doodh Ganga, are experiencing similar impacts.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: BBC Rests DIY SOS, Replaces with Spin-Off in 2027 Cost-Cutting Measure
cards.content: DIY SOS, a long-running home renovation TV series, will be rested in 2027 due to the BBC's savings challenges, and replaced by a spin-off show featuring highlights from past episodes. The decision comes as part of the corporation's drive to save £500m over three years, which has already led to the cancellation of several well-known TV shows. The BBC has confirmed that a new spin-off show, DIY SOS Rebuilt My Life, will revisit successful projects from the past and expand the brand on the BBC in a more cost-effective way. The original series, presented by Nick Knowles, has been airing since 1999 and has tackled numerous ambitious projects, including renovating homes for families facing severe illness, disability, or building disasters.

cards.title: Paul Shipper: From Film Fan to Illustrator of Marvel and Star Wars
cards.content: Paul Shipper, a film fan-turned-illustrator, has come a long way from creating movie poster artwork for fun. He has worked on some of Hollywood's biggest franchises, including Marvel, Indiana Jones, and Star Wars. Shipper's passion for illustration started when he was a kid, inspired by the films of George Lucas and Steven Spielberg. He shared his designs online, which led to opportunities that once seemed like a dream. The illustrator has worked on various projects, including posters and artwork for blockbuster titles, and has maintained a consistent artistic style despite working across different projects. Shipper is now involved in a charity exhibition, AMPjam Presents: We've Been Framed, which brings together more than 60 artists from around the world to create original artworks inspired by films and television shows.

cards.title: Scottish Actor Hopes Fans Accept His Accent in Marvel Series
cards.content: Scottish actor Ruaridh Mollica, who plays Tommy Maximoff in the Marvel Cinematic Universe miniseries VisionQuest, hopes fans will accept his Scottish accent. He says speaking in his own accent helped him bring the character to life, and he's excited to be part of the show.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: UK's Strong Growth Data Amid Global Economic Uncertainty
cards.content: A global economic tug-of-war is underway, with crises from energy shock, trade conflict, and war holding back growth, while massive AI spending and resilience from smaller economies pull in the other direction. At IMF meetings in Bangkok, finance ministers highlighted the UK's strong growth data and its model pupil status, but uncertainty remains about the future direction of the economy.

cards.title: Tesla Unveils Electric Sports Car with Hover Capabilities
cards.content: Tesla unveiled a new electric sports car that can hover and turn in mid-air, but it's unclear when flying cars will become a reality. Other news includes Meta's trial over claims its platforms are addictive, a ban on under-16s using social media, and the release of Nintendo's Switch 2. SpaceX's Starship rocket exploded during a test, and the US president is considering selling his Tesla car. A digital detox expert shares tips to help you stop looking at your phone.

cards.title: Small businesses increasingly adopt artificial intelligence tools
cards.content: Small businesses are adopting AI tools for customer support, marketing, document processing and data analysis. Lower-cost AI services are making technologies that were previously available mainly to large companies more accessible to smaller firms.
